liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Good Lovin'** (3 reviews): Reviewer singles out Good Lovin' among the strong versions in the second half, alongside Dark Star and the Not Fade Away combination; Described as exceptionally smooth, with Pigpen rapping for roughly twenty minutes and Jerry in rare form [7][8][10]
- **Drums** (2 reviews): Billy's drum solo is called one of his best, best appreciated within the roughly 40-minute Dark Star sequence [13][14]
- **Sugar Magnolia** (2 reviews): Reviewer considers this the best Sugar Magnolia ever, with Donna's vocals working well; Reviewer notes the original Sugar Magnolia vocals are unknown, apparently not preserved in this version [11][15]
- **Dark Star** (1 review): Reviewer especially loves the second-set Dark Star jam [9]
- **Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad** (1 review): The Not Fade Away into Goin' Down the Road sequence is called possibly the show's highlight [10]
- **Two Souls in Communion** (1 review): Reviewer calls this the finest version they have heard; Pigpen's songs stand out in the first half [7]

## The recordings

- **gd1972-05-04.sbd.miller.77294.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 29 songs; 205 min; rated 4.92/5 by 26 [1]. Said about its sound: The transfer is very clean, though the reviewer still treasures older analog board tapes of this show; Second-set disc changes are seamless, but cuts occur at the start of Casey Jones, end of Dark Star, and in Not Fade Away [1][15]
- **gd72-05-04.sbd.hamilton.143.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 29 songs; 205 min; rated 4/5 by 13 [2]
- **gd1972-05-04.152824.sbd.miller.sbeok.t-flac24**: soundboard; 29 songs; 205 min [3]
- **gd1972-05-04.sbd.set1.samaritano.20562.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 14 songs; 92 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [5]

## Around the show

- Power cuts out during Next Time You See Me, and the reviewer enjoys hearing it on the tape [8]
- The show includes five Pigpen songs, with his organ playing and singing praised by the reviewer [12]
- Reviewer lists the band members' ages at the time, from Keith at 23 to Phil at 32, while hearing Dark Star [17]
- Reviewer is surprised by the long show so soon after the previous night's, but slightly prefers this one [9]
- This Dark Star is enjoyable but does not match the 5/11 or 4/8 versions; the previous night is preferred [10]
- Reviewer says this is the source of the Europe '72 album version of Sugar Magnolia [11]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1972-05-04.sbd.miller.77294.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> (16 Track) Master Reel -> Dat D [1]. Also: Transfer made from a DAT lent by Steve Rolfe; Digital noise in Big Railroad Blues is patched from shnid 20562; Next Time You See Me comes from a different source [1]
- **gd72-05-04.sbd.hamilton.143.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD > reel > DAT > CDR [2]. Also: Chain is soundboard to reel to DAT to CDR, via J. Serafin and C. Gannon, with shn extraction by G.S. Hamilton [2]
- **gd1972-05-04.152824.sbd.miller.sbeok.t-flac24**: transferred by All Transfers and Mastering By Charlie Miller  September 6, 2006; source: SBD -> (16 Track) Master Reel -> Dat [3]. Also: This was one of the 'Honeymoon' tapes taken from David Gans's house while he was away on his honeymoon [3]
- **gd1972-05-04.sbd.set1.samaritano.20562.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Joe Samaritano; source: SBD > Master Reel [5]. Also: Patches in the first-set source come from an alternate soundboard, which keeps tuning and banter other copies edited out [5]
